tasks.short: Review service and delivery evidence and calculate the base charges due.

steps.what: Retrieve order details and service or delivery evidence.
Read supporting documents and identify billable quantities, dates and service codes.

loop.input: Supporting documents without usable structured fields.
loop.output: Billable items with document references and unresolved fields.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, dates, units and duplicates against order records; require evidence for each field.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved or contradictory fields enter the evidence exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use structured records first. Remaining documents contain variable layouts and free-text service descriptions.

steps.what: Find the applicable tariff and its effective dates.
Calculate base fees and check quantities against the supporting evidence.
Clarify missing service details and supply corrected evidence.
Approve exceptional fee interpretations or return them for more evidence.
Record supported base charges against the order.

tasks.design: An integration gathers billing evidence from the {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS}; a bounded extraction loop handles only documents without structured fields. Configured tariffs in the {ERP} calculate base charges, while a queue in the {WORKFLOW} routes missing evidence and exceptional fees to the responsible people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document layouts, service codes and tariff versions differ. Manual reading has bridged gaps between operational evidence and billing records.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured feeds and existing tariff configuration cover routine cases. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building adapters and a small validated extraction loop.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous service descriptions and disputed entitlement to charge remain difficult. Healthcare evidence may contain special-category personal data: GDPR requires an appropriate legal basis, strict access and data minimisation.
tasks.human_edge: A person establishes what service was actually delivered and whether an exceptional charge is defensible.

ambition.what: Charge previews for service coordinators using approved tariffs.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving weak evidence and explaining charge differences. A proposed delegation lets the clerk return incomplete submissions; fee exceptions remain with the billing supervisor.

reach.task: Compare billed service quantities with the quantities assumed in a quotation.
reach.learn: Service scope, measurement units and the difference between a tariff and an estimated cost.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit extracts invoice fields and identifies suppliers. This supports document capture feasibility, not clinical coding or customer fee interpretation.
Effective-dated tariffs, quantity checks and arithmetic can handle routine base-charge calculations deterministically.

assumptions: This task calculates base charges; contractual discounts and shipment adjustments belong to the separate billing-terms task.
Tariffs and service codes can be made explicit and versioned.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, including exception handling.
Build ranges cover one billing stream. The access range includes consultation under national rules where applicable; elapsed approval waits can be longer.
unknowns: Which source records are structured and which require document reading?
Does billing evidence contain health data or other special-category personal data?
Who may approve exceptional fees and return incomplete submissions?
Can the available interfaces create internal charges with source references?
research_questions: Which fields can be obtained directly before introducing document extraction?
How often do tariff selection and service-code interpretation disagree with a human review?
new_work: Review extracted billable items and resolve evidence exceptions.
Maintain tariff versions and service-code mappings.
Monitor duplicate imports and failed record writes.
Maintain access restrictions and extraction quality checks.

tasks.short: Compile cost-factor reports from labour, production, storage and equipment records.

steps.what: Export labour costs, production volumes, storage usage and equipment costs.
Combine extracts and reconcile periods, cost centres and measurement units.
Choose allocation treatments for shared costs and resolve unusual classifications.
Prepare cost tables and the report using the agreed allocation treatment.
Review totals and material movements before releasing the report.

tasks.design: Scheduled imports into the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile cost extracts from the {ERP}, {PAYROLL} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, with failed checks routed through the {WORKFLOW}. A deterministic generator produces the report in the {DOCS} and a drill-down view in the {BI}; the cost accountant approves allocation changes and report release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources use different periods, units and cost-centre mappings. Shared-cost allocations often depend on undocumented judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable mappings, reconciliation checks and report templates can now be assembled with less development effort. No model is needed for the proposed reporting path.
tasks.still_hard: A balanced report can still allocate costs misleadingly. Changes in production mix, capacity and allocation policy need accounting judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The cost accountant decides whether an allocation represents how resources were consumed.

ambition.what: Weekly review of unit-cost movements by service line.

tasks.altitude: The clerk investigates source differences and prepares explanations instead of assembling tables. A proposed delegation permits source-data queries to operational owners; allocation policy remains with the cost accountant.

reach.task: Separate volume changes from rate changes in service-line costs.
reach.learn: Cost drivers, fixed and variable costs, and variance decomposition.

evidence.claim: Scheduled extracts, mapping tables and deterministic report generation can automate recurring cost-report assembly.
Judgement remains necessary when shared-cost allocations lack a settled policy.

assumptions: The report supports billing and cost analysis rather than a complete statutory costing process.
Approved allocation treatments can be reused until policy or operating conditions change.
Aggregated labour costs are sufficient; individual employee records are excluded where unnecessary under GDPR.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one recurring report.
The access range includes employee consultation under national rules where applicable. Individual performance monitoring would require a separate GDPR and EU AI Act assessment.
unknowns: Are allocation policies documented and approved?
Do source periods and cost centres align?
Which labour-cost aggregation levels are available and permitted?
Who can approve report release and request operational corrections?
research_questions: Can existing reporting configuration produce the required report before custom generation is built?
Which reconciliations detect incomplete extracts and period-cutoff errors?
How sensitive are reported unit costs to alternative approved allocation methods?
new_work: Resolve failed imports and unmapped cost centres.
Maintain allocation versions, report definitions and source mappings.
Review material movements and approve report release.
Check that source changes do not expose unnecessary employee data.

tasks.short: Investigate accounting discrepancies, agree corrections and update the records.

steps.what: Retrieve disputed entries and related account transactions.
Compare amounts, references and dates to isolate unmatched or duplicate entries.
Read invoices and supporting documents to identify possible causes.

loop.input: A fixed case packet containing unmatched entries and their supporting documents.
loop.output: Evidence-linked possible causes, conflicting facts and missing evidence.
loop.check: Recompute amounts in code; validate every cited document and field; label unsupported causes as unresolved.
loop.stop: One analysis and one repair attempt per case; unresolved cases return to the billing clerk without a posting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact matching runs first. Remaining explanations can be scattered across free-text documents.

steps.what: Explain missing operational facts and provide supporting evidence.
Choose the proposed correction and record its accounting rationale.
Approve the correction, accounting period and supporting rationale.
Post the approved correction and attach the evidence.

tasks.design: Configured matching in the {ERP} isolates discrepancies using records from the {ERP} and {BANK}; a bounded loop reads the relevant evidence in the {DOCS} and drafts possible causes. A case queue in the {WORKFLOW} gathers missing facts, records the accountant's approval and posts only the approved correction through the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Identifiers do not always match, and the reason for a difference often sits outside the ledger. A matching rule cannot establish whether a charge was justified.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing matching configuration handles exact cases, while cheaper integrations assemble a complete case packet. A bounded reading loop can organise the remaining evidence without posting decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Missing delivery evidence, disputed facts and closed accounting periods still require people. Equal amounts alone do not establish a valid match.
tasks.human_edge: People establish the economic substance of the transaction and accept responsibility for the correction.

ambition.what: Monthly recurring billing-defect review for operational owners.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time on causes and corrective proposals. A proposed delegation allows the clerk to group recurring defects and request operational fixes; accounting approval remains with the accountant.

reach.task: Prepare an evidence-backed correction proposal with the appropriate accounting period.
reach.learn: Cutoff, materiality, reversals and the difference between a billing adjustment and a ledger correction.

reach.task: Identify recurring discrepancy causes by source process.
reach.learn: Consistent cause codes, denominators and measures of repeat occurrence.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports automatic bank matching using payment references, account identifiers or invoice numbers, with unmatched items requiring attention.
That matching capability supports routine reconciliation, but does not establish that arbitrary accounting discrepancies can be resolved automatically.
Evidence summaries can assist investigation when validated against source records; accounting corrections still require an authorised decision.

assumptions: The scope is billing-related discrepancies, not a full financial close.
Approval and posting permissions are separate and enforced.
Posting checks include balanced entries, valid periods, approval scope and duplicate prevention.
GDPR access and retention rules apply to case packets. Consultation under national rules is included where applicable.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one reconciliation process.
unknowns: Which discrepancy types dominate and which matching configuration already exists?
Which corrections require an accountant's approval under current policy?
Can the available interfaces enforce approval scope and prevent duplicate posting?
How often are source documents missing or inaccessible?
research_questions: What share of cases disappears after identifier and source-data repairs?
Can the case summary distinguish conflicting evidence from missing evidence reliably?
Which recurring causes can be prevented upstream?
new_work: Review evidence summaries and resolve unsupported explanations.
Maintain matching tolerances and discrepancy cause codes.
Handle rejected postings and approval changes.
Audit corrections and feed recurring defects back to operational owners.

tasks.short: Apply agreed credit terms, discounts and shipment rates to complete billing drafts.

steps.what: Check the customer's agreed payment terms and discount conditions.
Find the shipment tariff using destination, weight and service level.
Calculate discounts, shipment charges, due dates and billing totals.
Approve nonstandard discounts or payment terms and resolve conflicting conditions.
Enter the calculated amounts and approved adjustments into the billing draft.

tasks.design: Configure effective-dated payment terms, discounts, shipment tariffs and rounding rules in the {ERP}, using shipment facts from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A queue in the {WORKFLOW} captures nonstandard approvals and returns them to the {ERP}, which generates the billing draft with a calculation trace.
tasks.previous_blocker: Commercial conditions and shipment tariffs have not always been maintained as usable master data. A workbook often bridges that gap even when calculation features already exist.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration can perform most calculations. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of migrating rate tables, validating them and connecting shipment records.
tasks.still_hard: Contract precedence, retrospective rate changes and negotiated concessions remain difficult. An automated calculation cannot settle an ambiguous commercial agreement.
tasks.human_edge: The finance manager decides when a concession is justified and who may commit to changed terms.

ambition.what: Pre-dispatch checks for unexpected shipment surcharges.

tasks.altitude: The clerk investigates rate exceptions and explains calculations instead of rekeying totals. A proposed delegation lets the clerk hold incomplete drafts; nonstandard terms remain with the finance manager.

reach.task: Flag proposed payment terms that exceed an already approved account limit.
reach.learn: Exposure calculations, approval limits and escalation criteria without making a new creditworthiness decision.

evidence.claim: Contractual discounts, due dates and shipment-rate calculations are suitable for configured rules rather than model judgement.
The digest provides no directly documented outgoing-billing implementation or measured result for this task.

assumptions: This task applies approved credit terms; it does not assess creditworthiness or send invoices.
Commercial terms are available as structured master data. Unstructured contracts require a separate reviewed migration.
Existing configuration supports the required calculation sequence; gaps are confirmed before custom code is commissioned.
GDPR applies where customer records contain personal data. Expansion into natural-person creditworthiness assessment requires separate EU AI Act assessment.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one rate family. The access range includes consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which calculation features are already licensed and configured?
Are tariffs, discounts and contract precedence maintained centrally?
Who may approve concessions, and at what limits?
Which shipment facts arrive before the billing draft is prepared?
research_questions: Can existing configuration reproduce representative historical bills, including rounding and effective-date changes?
Which manual calculations remain after correcting master data?
Can surcharge exceptions be detected before dispatch using available shipment facts?
new_work: Maintain rate tables, effective dates and approval limits.
Review conflicting terms and missing shipment facts.
Verify representative calculations after tariff changes.
Monitor draft-generation failures and preserve calculation traces.

role.altitude: The role shifts from document reading, arithmetic and rekeying toward evidence quality, billing exceptions and recurring error prevention. Proposed authority covers returning incomplete submissions and holding unsupported drafts; pricing concessions, allocation policy and accounting approvals remain with designated finance roles.
reach: Cost estimators: compare delivered quantities with quoted scope.
Budget analysts: explain volume and rate movements in service costs.
Credit analysts: flag departures from approved terms and limits.
skills_to_grow: Evidence review, GDPR data minimisation and appropriate AI literacy.
role.ambitious_version: Run a billing-quality service that offers charge previews, detects shipment surcharges before dispatch and turns recurring discrepancies into specific operational fixes.
